title: Eviction policy and slow-drip traffic protocol (scratch)
content:
Purpose and quick context:
- Quick scratchpad for a tuned slow-drip deployment approach that emphasizes eviction safety, KV-cache warmup, and controlled backpressure for model variants that have memory/latency variance.
- This lives as my personal notes prior to formalizing into a playbook. Keep minimal steps that I can copy into runbooks.

High-level goal:
- Release new model variant X.v2 with minimal customer impact and predictable transient cost by:
  1) routing tiny steady trickle of traffic (0.05% -> 1%) to warm KV and kernel caches,
  2) evict aggressive sessions early (short RC-window) to avoid long-tail memory retention,
  3) progressively expand cohort size while verifying latency P95/P99 and error ratio.

Why this is different from standard canary:
- Traditional canary assumes quick stable latency; for large context models we need cache warmup and need to observe memory footprint changes over hours. Slow-drip avoids spiky pressure on GPU memory and autoscale.
- Adds explicit eviction policy (time-based + size-based) to avoid node-level OOMs when variant mismatches occur.

Core elements (quick checklist):
- Preflight:
  - Validate model artifact checksums and quantization profile (CLI: ./bin/check_model --id X.v2 --profile q4)
  - Confirm serving node image has testing hooks: /healthz/eviction and /metrics/kv_cache_hit
  - Deploy model to 2 isolated warm nodes (label: warm-witness) in eu-west1
  - Create temp rollout config in Console with initial traffic 0.05% and explicit max-concurrent-per-instance = 2

- Observability baseline (run 24h against baseline):
  - Record baseline P50/P95/P99 for model X.v1, error rate, GPU mem usage, KV cache hit rate
  - PromQL snippets to use:
    - error_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=runtime,handler=gen,model=~"X.*",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=runtime,handler=gen,model=~"X.*"}[5m]))
    - kv_hit = avg(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{model="X.v1"}[5m])) / avg(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{model="X.v1"}[5m]))
    - p95_lat = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{model=~"X.*"}[5m])) by (le))

- Launch plan (slow-drip phases):
  - Phase A: 0.05% steady traffic for 2 hours to warm caches (cohort type: synthetic / low-cost test keys)
  - Checkpoints after A: kv_hit > 25% OR no P99 spike > 2x baseline AND error_rate < 0.2%
  - Phase B: 0.5% for 6 hours (mix of synthetic + small real cohort, prefer org-internal users)
  - Phase C: 1% for 24 hours (wider cohort, monitor for memory pressure)
  - Phase D: ramp to 10% over 4h, then normal rollout cadence if stable

- Eviction policy (implementation notes):
  - Eviction triggers (order of precedence):
    1. hard OOM detection on node -> immediate redirect all X.v2 traffic from node and mark unschedulable
    2. sustained GPU memory usage > 85% for 5m plus P99 latency increased > 1.6x -> start selective session eviction
    3. KV-cache growth > configured quota (example: 12Gi per-instance) -> evict least-recently-used session keys older than 30m
  - Eviction tactic: graceful session eviction where in-flight requests finish but new requests for evicted sessions are routed to fallback variant X.v1 for 10 minutes
  - Fallback window and re-admit policy: after 10 minutes, session re-admitted to X.v2 at reduced token budget (for safety)

- Rollforward / rollback rules (automated + manual hooks):
  - Auto-rollback if:
    - P99 latency > 2x baseline for > 15m OR
    - error_rate increase > 1 percentage point for > 10m OR
    - GPU OOM observed on any warm node twice in 1h
  - Soft-fallback: route 90% of cohort to X.v1 but keep 10% to X.v2 for diagnostics instead of full rollback
  - Manual confirmation required for rollforward to >10% traffic (owner: Samira K or on-call eng-platform)

- Activation controls in Console/API:
  - Named policy: slow-drip-eviction-safe-v1
  - Config knobs: initial_weight, step_duration, max_weight, per-instance-concurrency, eviction_policy_id
  - Quick commands (examples):
    - set rollout weight: curl -X POST https://console/api/rollouts/slow-drip-eviction-safe-v1 -d '{"weight":0.005}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
    - emergency drain node: curl -X POST https://sre/api/nodes/drain -d '{"node": "node-45-eu"}'

- Post-activation checks (first 48h):
  - daily digest of: latency deltas, kv hit delta, token-cost per request, cost-per-1000 tokens for cohort
  - sanity check: no change in end-user error reports via Zendesk/Sentry driven alerts
  - schedule small retro after 72h with stakeholders: eng, product, infra, SRE

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want to persist eviction decisions to a lightweight audit log? (helpful for postmortem, small perf hit)
- Can we add an adaptive heatmap to Console showing per-session cache warmness? (visual ops tool)
- Should we pin X.v2 to a dedicated tiny pool for first 24h to isolate memory variance? Tradeoff: cost bump vs safer eviction surface.
- Verify whether autoscaler will spin new nodes for warm-witness label — tie to INF-3342.

Quick reminder for next time:
- Start warm-witness deployment at least 4h prior to Phase A for long-context models.
- Keep Slack channel #deploy-telemetry open and add short heartbeat messages every 30m during phases.

Scratch notes (commands, snippets):
- Promtail quick query: curl -G 'https://prometheus/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="X.v2"}[5m])) by (le))'
- Rapid rollback = set rollout weight 0 then squash warming cohorts.

End of scratch.

(If this becomes a formal doc: move to shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/ and split into playbook + admin-ops checklist.)
